title: Your Coding Agent Just Got Cloned And Your Brain Isn't Ready - Rustin Banks, Google Jules
talk_summary: Google Jules PM describes asynchronous parallel coding agents and best practices from early usage: define verifiable success, add tests first, run multiple candidate variations, use AI for task creation and merge/test bookends, keep repo docs as context, and run agents in cloud VMs. The demo shows parallel feature/test/audit work merged in about an hour, but most value is in workflow mechanics rather than product marketing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before starting, define how success will be verified and tell the agent not to stop until that check passes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: think before you get started, how am I going to easily verify that this works?

takeaways.what_they_do: First task adds or repairs tests and documents how to run them, so later parallel feature agents can self-check.
takeaways.evidence_quote: So, first we're going to add some tests.

takeaways.what_they_do: Clone a complex task across agents with different approaches or libraries, then choose the winner by a measurable criterion like test coverage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Try it this way, try it that way, or give me this variation to look at

takeaways.technique: AI bookends for task creation and merge
takeaways.what_they_do: Use agents to turn backlog and bug reports into tasks, and critic/merge agents to integrate and test parallel work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI can easily work through backlogs, bug reports to create tasks for you

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain MD files and links to documentation with test instructions so agents can retrieve needed context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Keep using MD files or links to documentation

takeaways.what_they_do: Run each async agent in its own cloud VM with a full repo clone and command execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Jules now has its own VM in the cloud
